circuits.name: Klon Centaur
circuits.description: The Klon Centaur splits the signal into a clean path and a germanium-diode overdrive path and mixes them back together in an op-amp summing stage run from an ICL7660 charge pump (about 18V, plus a negative rail), so the mixer never clips. A dual-gang Gain pot raises the overdrive gain while lowering the clean blend, and the Treble control is an active treble boost/cut. The author built one on a toner-transfer PCB in a Hammond BB box and found it a nice booster but only an OK overdrive, planning a version with separate gain and blend pots and a different op amp (an LF353) in the drive stage.
notes: The author suggests separate Gain and Blend pots in place of the dual-gang pot, a diode blend pot to mix two clipping voices, and an LF353 in place of the TL072 in the buffer/overdrive section.

circuits.name: Revolution Deux L'Overdrive de la Revolution Deux (LORD)
circuits.original: Fred Briggs L'Overdrive de la Revolution Deux (LORD)
circuits.description: The blog author's own overdrive, designed for the freestompboxes forum: a BS170 MOSFET gain stage, a passive tone control, then two cascaded J201 JFET stages that clip. The tone control sits between the MOSFET and JFET stages so it shapes the harmonics of the clipping stages, and a DPDT switch can bypass it for a large gain boost. The author describes it as somewhere between a Marshall and a Mesa, more open and touch sensitive at 12V or 18V.
notes: C2 (MOSFET output cap) sets the bass response; values from 2.2n to 22n work. The author used 4.7n in his build with a 'voice' switch that adds another 4.7n in parallel (thin vs stock).
C7 (10u on Q2's source): remove it for lower gain, or replace it with 100n for a 'presence' boost; the author used 100n in his build.
C5 (1n on Q2's gate): increase for more high-end roll-off.
C8 (470p): alter for more high-end roll-off; 220p to 1n work well.
C10 (470n presence cap on Q3's source): change the value to alter the frequency response.
Alternate tone stack (used in the author's build): 10n, two 10K resistors, a B50K pot, 82n and 1K.
The PCB version by Marshmellow adds a Gain switch that lifts C7.
Try running it at 9V, 12V and 18V; higher voltage gives a more open, less compressed tone.

circuits.name: Lovepedal Eternity Burst
circuits.description: A de-gooped Lovepedal Eternity, which the post shows is a modified version of Jack Orman's Son of a Screamer: a minimal Tube Screamer with one op-amp half as the clipping gain stage (four diodes, two in series each way, in the feedback loop) and the other half as a buffer after a passive tone control. The author built it on perfboard as his 'Lovestuff Ecstasy Overdrive', with Drive, Level and Glass (a standard tone control) on the panel.
notes: The vero layout notes the gain pot is 500k, sometimes 1M.

circuits.name: Revolution Deux Clock of Tone 50
circuits.description: Fred Briggs' modified Lovepedal COT50 (Church of Tone 50), a single-transistor 2N5088 booster with a pair of clipping diodes to ground at the output. He raised the input and output caps (47n/100n to 56n/120n) for more bass, swapped the 1N60 diodes for softer 1N270 germanium diodes, added a 47n cap across the diodes to tame the fizz, and added a Nature pot that blends from a full boost to a Rangemaster-style treble boost beside the original Structure (gain) control.
notes: Reduce the 47n cap across the diodes (C6) for more highs.
The Electric Church Pedal variant adds a 470k master volume pot at the end of the circuit and a pot (about 10k) controlling the diodes' clipping threshold.
A reader's sound sample compares BC108 and 2N5088 transistors at low, medium and full gain.

circuits.name: Revolution Deux L'Overdrive de la Révolution Trois
circuits.original: Fred Briggs L'Overdrive de la Révolution Trois
circuits.description: Fred Briggs' light overdrive/booster, the third in his L'Overdrive de la Révolution series. The front end is a J201 JFET stage borrowed from runoffgroove's Omega booster, with its Range control reused here as a 'Body' control, feeding a pair of 1N34A germanium diodes to ground and then a BS170 MOSFET gain stage. It is meant to be driven straight from the guitar, with the guitar's volume and tone knobs shaping the gain and tone; there is not much clean headroom.
notes: A B100K pot can be used for Body: slightly less range but more control.
Substitute an A500K pot for Drive for more gain.
Lower the 820R MOSFET source resistor (R9) for more gain in the MOSFET section.
Adjust the 100K trimmer until the voltage across the J201's 100K drain resistor is 4.5-7V: 4.5V gives a fat round sound, 7V more grit. Try different JFETs for more sounds.

Alternate clipping section (the author's own build): a 22n series cap and 100n to ground ahead of the 1N34A diodes, for clean lows and clipped highs; the 22n sets the bass fed to the clippers and the 100n the highs. Torchy's layout shows a switch between the two clipping sections.

circuits.name: Landgraff Dynamic Overdrive (drawn by Clay Jones)
circuits.description: Clay Jones's hand drawing of the Landgraff Dynamic Overdrive ('Grand Laff Dynamic Overtype'), a TS808 replica: 2SC1815 input and output buffers around a JRC4558 Tube Screamer clipping stage and tone control. A three-way switch picks TS808 diodes, no diodes, or LED 'Marshall' clipping.
notes: SW1 (SPDT on/none/on): up is TS808 (1N914 diodes), center lifts the diodes, down is 'Marshall' (LEDs).
The drawing lists Blue Nichicon filter caps, a Sprague buffer cap, AVX polyester box NP caps, 1/4W carbon comp resistors.

circuits.name: Clay Jones Overdrive / Black Market Overdrive
circuits.description: The degooped Clay Jones Overdrive / Black Market Overdrive, which the post shows is a TS808 clone by way of the Landgraff Dynamic Overdrive: BC546B input and output buffers, an OPA2134 Tube Screamer clipping stage with red LED clippers, and the standard tone control. Freestompboxes member Whammy opened one up.
notes: The post says to use 5mm red LEDs for the clippers and an OPA2134 op-amp to get the CJOD sound.

circuits.name: Revolution Deux Son of a Clay Jones Overdrive
circuits.description: The blog author's simplification of the Clay Jones Overdrive, itself revealed as a Landgraff Dynamic Overdrive / Tube Screamer 808 variant. Following Jack Orman's Son of a Screamer, the input and output transistor buffers are removed; the rest is the CJOD: a non-inverting OPA2134 gain stage with red LEDs in the feedback loop, then the Tube Screamer tone control and volume. The author finds it sounds as good as or better than the original with fewer parts.
notes: The drawing stresses that the OPA2134 op-amp and the red LED clippers are essential.

circuits.name: Vsex Pedals Proximity Sensor (Zvex Probe controller)
circuits.description: A redrawn version of the proximity controller in Zvex's Probe pedals, as revealed by freestompboxes.org members (~arph and others): an antenna plate feeds a 2N3906 oscillator built around 4093 NAND gates, whose output drives a 2N3904 LED driver lighting a vactrol. The vactrol's LDR then controls a parameter of an effect, here the Colorsound wah.
notes: A copper board blank used for etching PCBs works as the antenna; try different sized plates.
Use the 250KA pot to tune the sensitivity to a given antenna size and shoe thickness; the 10KA sets the starting intensity of the LED.
When first tuning the circuit, use a visible LED in place of the vactrol to see how it reacts, then change to the vactrol.

circuits.name: Colorsound Inductorless Wah (Vsex FX mods)
circuits.description: The old inductorless Colorsound wah, a single transistor with a twin-T style feedback network, which Zvex uses with mods in his Ooh-Wah, Seek-Wah and Wah-Probe. Here the wah pot is replaced by the LDR of the proximity controller's vactrol to make a Wah Probe work-alike.
notes: Replace the 33K resistor with a 50KB pot for a 'resonance' control, from standard wah to squealing self-oscillation.
The original unit uses a TN326 transistor; many NPN transistors work, and the author used a 2N3904.

circuits.name: Analogman King of Tone (one channel)
circuits.description: One half of the Analogman King of Tone, which the author calls a modified Marshall Bluesbreaker: a JRC4580 input buffer, a non-inverting gain stage with MA856 diode pairs in its feedback loop (switched by DIP1), 1S1588 diodes to ground (DIP2), and a Bluesbreaker-style tone with a treble-boost trimmer. The KOT puts two of these in series; Torchy's General Guitar Gadgets project builds one half, so build two for the full pedal.
notes: The drawing lists changed values for the General Guitar Gadgets project boards only: R2 27K, R3 33K, R7 a jumper, C5 100u electrolytic, C6 a jumper, C7 100n, plus an added 10K gain stopper resistor, a 50K treble-boost trimmer and a 1u output cap.

circuits.name: Paul Cochrane Timmy
circuits.description: Paul Cochrane's Timmy transparent overdrive: a JRC4559 op-amp gain stage with 1N4148 clipping diodes in its feedback loop (a DIP switch selects symmetric or asymmetric pairs), a passive Bass cut control ahead of the gain stage, a Treble cut low-pass after it, and a second op-amp stage with fixed 2x gain driving the Volume pot. It has been cloned widely, by the Danelectro Cool Cat Transparent OD and the Lovepedal Amp Eleven and OD Eleven among others.
notes: Feedback mod (image 3): a 47K resistor and a DPDT on/off/on toggle choosing 2.2n or 220n from the output back to the input, as in the BJF Honeybee and the author's Hummingbird, lowers the overall gain and brightness.

Clipping options (image 4): a 2PDT footswitch and an on/off/on toggle between the op amp's inverting input (point A) and output (point B) choose among 1N4148, 1N270, 1N34A, 1N5818 and BS170 MOSFET clippers.

Paul Cochrane advises that with other diodes, LEDs or no diodes the output stage should be turned into a unity-gain buffer (or have its gain switched with the diodes) to avoid rail clipping; with no diodes the first stage swings from a gain of 2 to about 304 with the 1M Drive pot.
twangquack found nearly every op amp works; he liked a TL072 with an OPA2134 stacked on top, and an RC4559 alone sounded darker with nice drive.

circuits.name: Hermida Audio Zendrive (Z-Drive project by stratotrasto)
circuits.description: A complete DIY project of the Hermida Audio Zendrive by freestompboxes member stratotrasto, with schematic, PCB layout and a drilling template. The Zendrive is a dual op-amp overdrive whose feedback loop clips through two 2N7000 MOSFETs and Schottky/germanium diodes, with a Voice control setting the low end of the gain stage, followed by a passive tone filter and a buffered output.
notes: The schematic lists alternatives: MBR040 or 1N34A for D1, D2 and D3, and a Burr-Brown OPA2604 for IC1.
The schematic suggests audio taper pots for Voice, Gain and Tone.

circuits.name: Jetter Gain Stage Red
circuits.description: Jetter's Gain Stage Red, traced by Soulsonic (Martin Chittum), is almost an exact clone of the Hermida Zendrive. The Voice pot is replaced by a Hard/Soft switch choosing between two fixed resistors in the same voice network, the 100pF feedback cap is gone, the Tone pot is 100K linear instead of 50K, and a reverse polarity diode is added.
notes: Any dual op-amp should work for U1 (its markings were sanded off); AD712 and OPA2604 are reported to work well.
Q1 and Q2 are N-channel enhancement MOSFETs, likely 2N7000 or BS170.

circuits.name: Skreddy Mayo
circuits.description: Skreddy's take on the Electro-Harmonix Big Muff, voiced after the Muff sound of the Smashing Pumpkins' 'Siamese Dream' (named for the song 'Mayonaise'). It is a four-transistor (2N5133) Big Muff with R19 and C5 swapped from the standard order and added CX and RX parts. The designer stresses using the exact part types specified (carbon composition resistors, ceramic capacitors, metal film for C5-C7); the post's author found it one of the best Muff variants he had breadboarded.
notes: The tone stack shown is the classic mid scoop; for flat mids, replace C8 and C9 both with 5.6n.
Skreddy Pink Flesh work-alike (per Marc): C1 10u, C8 4.7n, CX 220p-470p, C3 68n, a switch to put 4.7n in parallel with C9 for a mid boost, and a 100 ohm resistor after DX (plus transistor selection).
The vero layout adds a three-position scooped/flat/boosted mids switch using 4.7n and 10n capacitors.
The 3PDT footswitch is wired to ground the input in bypass (not shown).

circuits.name: ZVex Machine
circuits.description: Zachary Vex's Machine, a distortion built from two cascaded frequency-tripler stages that distort through crossover distortion, in the sloped middle of the waveform rather than at the peaks. Each stage is a BS170 MOSFET gain stage (the first a Super Hard On, so the In knob acts as a drive) feeding a complementary 2N3906/2N3904 pair. A Limit control sets a pair of diodes that clip the original waveform down to about the size of the harmonics. It is meant to stack in front of other fuzzes rather than for chords.
notes: Traced from a 2001 unit with no LED or power jack; if you add a power jack, add some power filtering to prevent 60Hz hum.

circuits.name: Tim Escobedo Tripple Fuzz
circuits.description: Tim Escobedo's Tripple Fuzz, built around a 'nonselective frequency tripler' originally designed by R. Lockhart Jr.: an MPSA18 gain stage feeds a complementary 2N3906/2N3904 pair, followed by silicon diodes to ground. The drawing says it is sweet at low gain, an odd splatty fizz as the gain rises and nasty at full gain. The post shows it as the same tripler structure the Machine uses (and the Lovepedal Karl).

circuits.name: Xotic AC Booster
circuits.description: The Xotic AC Booster, a well-loved booster/overdrive. A 2SC1815 emitter-follower input buffer feeds a 4557 op-amp clipper with 1N4148 diodes in its feedback loop (two on one side, one on the other), and the less usual addition the post points out: an active Baxandall tone stack on the second half of the op-amp after the clipping, followed by a volume pot and a 2SC1815 output buffer.
notes: Kusi's mods to turn the AC Booster into an RC Booster: C1 = 47n; C2 = 1u non-polar; remove R8 and bridge it; remove C4; R5 = 22K; R7 = 250K; clipping diodes 3x 1N4148 on each side.

circuits.name: Mad Professor Little Green Wonder
circuits.description: Bjorn Juhl's (BJF) overdrive for Mad Professor, conceived as his take on a Tube Screamer-style pedal with more headroom, less bass and low-mid cut, and treble filtering that suits humbuckers and P-90s. A 2SK170 JFET input buffer feeds a TLC272 op amp whose first half clips through two green LEDs in its feedback loop; the second half is a gain stage, and the unusual Body control is a dual 20k pot working in both stages.
notes: The first LGWs used an LF353 op amp for more headroom; later ones use the TLC272, which works at lower voltages and distorts more easily.

circuits.name: Fulltone OCD V4 (Stratotrasto)
circuits.description: Stratotrasto's schematic and PCB of the Fulltone OCD version 4, an amp-like overdrive with a TL082 gain stage, a pair of 2N7000 MOSFETs (and a 1N34 germanium diode) clipping to ground, a second op-amp gain stage and a passive tone with a high/low-pass switch. The post points out it is essentially a modified Voodoo Lab Overdrive.
notes: Check that the pinout of your clipping MOSFETs matches the layout.
The germanium diode (1N34) can be left out: it was on the V4 prototype but dropped from the newest models.
The author's redesigned Super OCD is a further option.

circuits.name: HAO Rust Driver
circuits.description: A HAO overdrive said to emulate a 1969 Marshall Plexi 50W turned up to 10. It is a simple dual op-amp circuit: an inverting gain stage, then a second inverting stage with silicon clipping diodes, a 470K resistor and a 1.2n cap in its feedback, an output divider and a volume pot.
notes: Any dual op-amp such as an LF353 or LF412 can be used.
The clipping diodes are silicon, e.g. 1SS119.

circuits.name: Baldwin-Burns Buzzaround
circuits.description: The sought-after Burns Buzzaround, a three-PNP-germanium fuzz researched by Dragonfly of Soulkitchen FX, David Main of D*A*M and others. A direct-coupled two-transistor amplifier feeds a germanium-diode-biased distortion stage, with Balance setting the bias of the third transistor and Timbre a simple tone control at the output. The post notes it is very similar to the old three-knob Tone Benders.
notes: David Main (D*A*M) reports seeing a 10K Balance pot instead of 5K.
David Main reports seeing a 24K resistor (R1) instead of 27K.

circuits.name: Mictester Burns Buzzaround-Alike
circuits.description: Mictester's sound-alike of the Buzzaround that needs only one germanium transistor. A TL072 op-amp gain stage replaces the original two-transistor amplifier, the heart is the original germanium distortion stage (with an NPN 2N1302), and the second op-amp half buffers the tone circuit so Timbre works over its full range. The author preferred it to his Buzzaround clone.
notes: You can raise the first stage's gain by increasing its 100K feedback resistor (R4).
Use a 2N1302 with an hFE of about 80 and a bit of leakage for it to work properly.

circuits.name: Lovepedal Purple Plexi
circuits.description: The Lovepedal Purple Plexi, traced by the freestompboxes.org community (schematic by Ghandi). The post calls it a simple LM386 power-amp-chip distortion: a JRC386D with a gain pot between pins 1 and 8, followed by a passive low-pass and a Freq control before the volume pot.

circuits.name: Lovepedal Purple Plexi 800
circuits.description: The Purple Plexi 800, which the post describes as a slight variation on the Purple Plexi LM386 distortion. Going by the vero layout's parts list, the differences are a 100p input capacitor and 22n in place of the two 4.7n capacitors (C2 and C6).

circuits.name: Lovepedal Woodrow
circuits.description: Lovepedal's one-knob Woodrow, sold as a cranked 5E3 Tweed tone, is in the author's view just an Electra Distortion: a single 2N5088 common-emitter stage with collector-to-base feedback bias and a bypassed emitter resistor, followed by a pair of 1N914 diodes clipping to ground and a 500K volume pot.

circuits.name: Menatone King of the Britons
circuits.description: Menatone's King of the Britons, a Marshall-style high-gain distortion from the maker known for amp-in-a-can pedals. The schematic shows six J201 JFET stages modeling a tube preamp: three cascaded gain stages with a Gain pot, a source follower driving a Marshall-type High/Mid/Low tone stack, then a Master pot and two more JFET stages before the Level control. The author liked it but preferred runoffgroove's Thor.

circuits.name: Kustom Kretin Drive (G2D Custom Cream Tone)
circuits.description: A hand-drawn schematic titled 'Kustom Kretin Drive' (freestompboxes.org, signed Briggs), posted beside a photo of the G2D (Good to Do) Custom Overdrive / Custom Cream Tone with the hint that the two are related. The drawing shows several op-amp stages in cascade, with a 'Crunch' section, a 'Hammer' section and a 'Madder' control, and switches for the pedal's Blues and Solo modes.

circuits.name: Fred Briggs Fuzz
circuits.description: The author's take on the Fuzz Face: a silicon two-stage feedback fuzz whose first stage is a piggybacked (Darlington-style) pair with a 100K trimmer to set its gain, a Sag pot that limits the voltage on the clipping transistor, and BAT46 diodes after the output with a Compression pot that sets their clipping threshold. It ranges from light overdrive to spitting fuzz depending on the guitar volume and Sag setting.
notes: The 10n capacitor across the 4K7 collector resistor is optional and rolls off extra highs.
Adjust the 100K trimmer so Q1 has a gain of about 25.

circuits.name: Fred Briggs Overdrive
circuits.description: The blog author's own light overdrive and booster, which he describes as a mix of the ZVex Super Hard On, the Lovepedal COT50 and his own ideas: a single 2N7000 or BS170 MOSFET gain stage with a red LED in its bias network, germanium diode clipping to ground at the output, and two 1KB controls in the source leg. Structure sets the overall gain; Nature is a subtle, interactive mid/high control.
notes: The drawing suggests adding a switch in series with the clipping diodes to remove the diode clipping.

circuits.name: Nick Greer Green Giant
circuits.description: Nick Greer's overdrive, formerly built by Greer Amplification for endorsers only. It is an Electra Distortion: one 2N3904 stage with collector-to-base feedback bias, followed by a pair of 1N4148 clipping diodes to ground, with a 25k Clean Mix pot added in series with the diodes to raise the clipping threshold so more clean signal comes through.

circuits.name: EMMA ReezaFRATzitz RF-1
circuits.description: EMMA's RF-1 distortion, built from the inverters of a CD4069 CMOS chip run as cascaded gain stages, in the spirit of the 'Tube Sound Fuzz'. Its Bias control moves the stages between class B and class A biasing to change the harmonic structure, and a hi boost/hi cut tone stage follows. The author built it and found it more dynamic than a Rat, cleaning up well with the guitar volume.
notes: This project includes a 'Bass/mids' mod that the post says adds a lot of tones and is well worth doing.

circuits.name: Revolution Deux Mixer/Switching System
circuits.description: Fred Briggs' wet/dry mixer and effects-loop switcher, built to rehouse a Behringer RM600 Reverb Machine running 100% wet. A Super Hard On style BS170 MOSFET preamp with a Pregain control buffers the input, the wet path goes out and back through a loop with two-pole low-pass filtering to soften the reverb's noise, and TL084 buffers isolate the dry and wet paths before they are summed with Dry Level and Wet Level controls; the fourth op-amp makes the half-supply bias. He notes it works for other bargain digital pedals too, such as the Behringer EM600 Echo Machine.
notes: Use switched jacks for the FX loop.
The drawing suggests dual outputs for a 'stereo' wet and dry out, and a switched jack for the wet signal.

circuits.name: Landgraff Dynamic Overdrive
circuits.description: A Tube Screamer (JRC4558, 2SC1815 input and output buffers) with a three-position toggle that selects the clipping in the feedback loop: TS808-style silicon diodes, no diodes (diode lift), or a pair of red LEDs for a 'Marshall' setting. The post jokes about its familiarity and suggests comparing it with the Clay Jones Overdrive, since Clay Jones drew this schematic.

circuits.name: Skreddy Screwdriver v1.2
circuits.description: The Screwdriver from Marc at Skreddy Pedals, a very dynamic, natural-sounding transistor overdrive, as dissected at freestompboxes.org. The post shares Cow4prez's drawing of version 1.2.

circuits.name: BJF Dyna Red Distortion
circuits.description: Bjorn Juhl's Dyna Red: a CA3130 op-amp gain stage with two red LEDs clipping in the feedback loop, a 1N4001 diode pair to ground after it, a treble control, and a 2N5458 JFET buffer before the volume. A 470p cap feeds the output back to the input stage to lower high-frequency gain. Smooth top end and a dynamic response.
notes: The author suggests adding the bass control from Paul C's Timmy.

circuits.name: Bearfoot FX Dyna Red Distortion
circuits.description: The Bearfoot FX production version of the Dyna Red, shown as an edit of the BJF trace: the same CA3130 stage with red LED clipping, diode pair, treble control and 2N5458 buffer, with a larger 47n input cap, 14.7K input resistor, 220p feedback cap, 3.6K and 3K resistors in place of the 3K and 4.7K, and the 6.8K/10u leg removed.

circuits.name: Catalinbread Dirty Little Secret
circuits.description: A Marshall-in-a-box overdrive made of stacked JFET mu-amp stages (six 2N5457s) with a source-follower between them, a DPDT toggle that changes the voicing caps, and a passive tone filter before the volume. The author notes that stacked mu-amps react strongly to supply voltage: articulate and dynamic at 18V, softer and more compressed as it drops.
notes: The author plans an adjustable supply from 18V down to 4.5V for his build, as the mu-amp stages sound very different across that range.

circuits.name: Fred Briggs Hummingbird Overdrive De'luxe
circuits.description: The blog author's own low-gain overdrive, which he describes as an enhancer that makes a good overdrive tone better. It came from a challenge by Bjorn of BJF to build something that sounds like the BJF Honey Bee: a 2SK117/2SK170 JFET input with a germanium MP14B, Schottky and MOSFET clipping set by the Compression control, 1N4001 diodes in the Shimmer network, and a BS170 MOSFET output stage. The Compression and Shimmer controls interact strongly with the gain, clipping and overall feel.
notes: Point B goes to the input of the MOSFET (BS170) stage.

circuits.name: Fred Briggs Silver Orchid Overdrive
circuits.description: The author's own overdrive and boost (2009), a development of his standard overdrive: a single BS170 MOSFET gain stage with Schottky diode clipping after it and a charge pump to run it above 9V. The drawing calls it ultra dynamic, responsive to the guitar's volume pot, and a flat boost into a cranked amp.
notes: Add a switch to the clipping diodes for extra fun.

circuits.name: Blackstone Appliances Mosfet Overdrive
circuits.description: A two-channel overdrive: an MPF102 JFET and TL072 op-amp front end feeding CD4049UBE CMOS inverter gain stages (each inverter is a pair of MOSFETs), with separate drive and level controls for the red and brown/blue channels and a mid cut. The post says it sounds tube-like and very responsive, a change from the Tube Screamer.
notes: VR6 (500K trim) sets stage 2 treble and VR7 (500K trim) stage 2 gain.
C11 and the PCL 330p cap are socketed for experimenting.

circuits.name: ToneCzar Openhaus
circuits.description: A brutal, complex 18V distortion from ToneCzar, reverse engineered at freestompboxes.org (credited to abfackeln). Four OPA2604 op-amps, LND150 depletion MOSFETs, a 2N5457 JFET and a pair of 2N1306 germanium transistors, with a three-band EQ, gain-mode, phase and mid-voicing switches and an expression pedal input. The post links the schematic and parts list and a PCB, and shows a verified vero layout.

circuits.name: BJF Honeybee Overdrive
circuits.description: Bjorn Juhl's low-gain overdrive inspired by an old Supro amp, reverse engineered on freestompboxes. A CA3130 op-amp gain stage with green LED clipping in its feedback, feedback loops that shape the high end, a filter at the end of the circuit and a 2N5457 JFET output stage. The post found it a great slightly-dirtier-than-a-booster pedal into a tube amp on the edge of breakup, very dynamic.
notes: Bearfoot Honeybee variant: C5 on the madbean schematic is 220n and is in series with a 4.7K resistor.

circuits.name: Hot Rodded Honey Bee (a la Honey Bee Deluxe)
circuits.original: BJFE / Bearfoot Fx Hot Rodded Honey Bee
circuits.description: A Honeybee with extras in the manner of the Honey Bee Deluxe, cobbled together from the Model-H, Blueberry and Honeybee schematics. A BF244A JFET boost stage with a Boost control feeds the CA3130 Honeybee core with LED clipping, then a 1N4007-clipped filter with a Treble control and a BF244A output stage.

circuits.name: Mad Professor Fire Red Fuzz
circuits.description: A Big Muff derivative with BC550C stages: an input boost, a pot-controlled fuzz level, then two clipping stages, the first clipped by a pair of 2N3819 JFETs used as diodes and the second by 1N4148s. A Big Muff-style tone stack is followed by a 2N5485 JFET output stage.

circuits.name: Mad Professor Sweet Honey Overdrive
circuits.description: A touch-sensitive medium-gain overdrive designed by Bjorn Juhl (BJFe) for Mad Professor, in the vein of his Honey Bee. An OP275 gain stage with red LEDs clipping in its feedback loop feeds a 1N4007 diode clipper and a passive network with the Focus control, which sets feel, dynamics and overall EQ, then a second op amp stage with LED clipping and the Volume pot.

circuits.name: ZVex Fuzz Factory
circuits.description: Zachary Vex's Fuzz Factory: a 2N3904 input stage feeding a germanium AC128 pair in a Fuzz Face style arrangement, with five interactive controls including Stab, a series supply-starving pot, and Gate, Comp and Drive pots that move the bias. It is known for wild oscillating and gated sounds as well as usable fuzz once tuned.
notes: Some units use 2N404 instead of AC128.
The vero layout notes that BC558 silicon transistors work well in place of Q1 and Q2.

circuits.name: Bearfoot FX Model H
circuits.description: Bjorn Juhl's Model H for Bearfoot FX, voiced after a Hiwatt amp. A 2N5952 JFET input stage with the Drive pot in its source feeds a CA3130 op-amp stage with red LED clipping in its feedback loop, then a JFET stage with a tone network and a JFET output stage. The post notes it is almost the same structure as BJF's Mad Professor Blueberry, or a hot-rodded Honey Bee.
notes: The vero layout suggests replacing R15 with a 5K pot or trimmer for a treble control.

circuits.name: Bigfoot FX MagnaVibe
circuits.description: Bigfoot FX's vibrato inspired by the early-1960s Magnatone amp vibrato (the newer version without the tremolo switch). It is a single MPSA18 phase-shift stage whose LDR is pulsed by an LED driven from a transistor phase-shift LFO; the post notes it is very close to Tim Escobedo's Wobbletron, with the LED/LDR replacing the JFET.
notes: For a more complex version with many more tones, the post points to MadBeanPedals' QuadraVibe project.

circuits.name: Tim Escobedo Wobbletron
circuits.description: Tim Escobedo's simple vibrato (v0.9, 08/04): one MPSA18 phase-shift stage whose shift is varied by a J201, driven by Darren Inwood and Rob Strand's pulsing-LED phase-shift oscillator. The post shows it because the MagnaVibe is nearly the same circuit with an LED/LDR in place of the JFET.
notes: C1 can be changed in value for a different vibrato tone.
More audio phase-shift stages can be added for a more dramatic effect.

circuits.name: BJF Sea Blue EQ
circuits.description: Bjorn Juhl's EQ booster with light distortion, meant to fine-tune the in-between bands that amp tone controls miss. It is a James-style passive bass/treble network between two JFET gain stages. The post warns that op-amps could replace the JFET stages only if the output impedance driving the EQ stays the same, since it shapes the tone section's response.
notes: The JFETs are unknown; 2N5458 or 2N5452 bias to the correct voltages (the vero layout uses 2N5458).
The vero layout suggests a higher value for R1 if the LED is too bright.

circuits.name: Carl Martin PlexiTone (rev. 3)
circuits.description: A three-mode overdrive (crunch, high gain and an up to 20 dB clean boost) built on an LF347 quad op-amp: an input buffer, an op-amp gain stage with LED clippers in the feedback loop and switchable Crunch and Hi-Gain pots, a tone stage, and a separate boost stage. The onboard transformer and 7812/7912 regulators give +/-12V, so the op-amp never clips and all the distortion comes from the LEDs.
notes: Values in red on the drawing are from early units (provided by JHS): C7 47p instead of 330p, C13 100n instead of 68n, R7 15K instead of 22K; LED4 is also circled as an early-unit difference.
Bucksears' PCB layout (Plexituna) runs from 9V with an LT1054 voltage doubler for +/-18V rails and omits the boost stage.

circuits.name: Catalinbread Formula No. 5
circuits.description: Catalinbread's overdrive inspired by the tweed 5E3 amp: two cascaded 2N5457 'mu-amp' stages with a gain and tone section between them, much like the Catalinbread Dirty Little Secret. The post credits the deliberately mis-biased first stage with its asymmetrical clipping harmonics.

circuits.name: Catalinbread Super Charged Overdrive (SCOD)
circuits.description: A high-gain overdrive that gets its gain and clipping from cascaded MOSFET stages instead of diodes: two BS170 boost stages sandwich a CD4007 logic chip wired as further cascaded inverter gain stages, five gain stages in all. The CD4007 section is essentially Gez's late-1990s Nut Cruncher. A Contour control sits in the feedback path and the output passes through a two-pole RC filter to the Volume pot.

circuits.name: Gez Nut Cruncher
circuits.description: A late-1990s design by Gez that uses the MOSFETs inside a CD4007 as three cascaded inverter gain stages, each biased with 1M feedback resistors and filtered with small caps. Mictester pointed out that it is what sits inside the Catalinbread SCOD's CD4007 section. Draws about 5mA.

circuits.name: Crowther Hotcake (1977)
circuits.description: Paul Crowther's Hotcake, first made in 1976: a single LM741 op-amp pushed into clipping, followed by a passive RC low-pass ladder and a Mid Lift/Normal switch that takes the output either after the filter or from a mid-boosted tap. Bajaman finds the 1977 version smoother and more Marshall-like than the newer one.

circuits.name: Crowther Hotcake (2003)
circuits.description: The 2003 Hotcake: the same clipped op-amp core (a TL071, LM741 on older units) with an 8.2V zener-regulated supply, a Presence control in place of the Mid Lift switch, and bistable-relay switching. Bajaman hears it as glassier and more Fender-like than the 1977 version.
notes: Per the drawing, Presence (P2) may be 50K linear on later units, and older units use an LM741.

circuits.name: D*A*M Meathead
circuits.description: A one-knob silicon Fuzz Face (2N3904 and BC182L) with small caps from the collectors back to the bases that smooth the fuzz. The post says transistor selection makes a huge difference and suggests trying different types.
notes: Try different transistor types for new tones.

circuits.name: D*A*M Meathead Deluxe M-25
circuits.description: The deluxe Meathead adds a bias trimmer and a 'Filter' control, an input blend that sets the low-end response, while 'Attack' is the usual Fuzz Face fuzz control. It uses a BC337-16 and a BC107B.
notes: Set the 22K trimmer for 4.5V on Q2's collector.
C4 can be 4n7 or 5n6.

circuits.name: Death by Audio Robot
circuits.description: A lo-fi 8-bit pitch shifter built around the Holtek HT8950 voice modulator chip, with a TL072 input gain stage and output stage and a split supply from two 3.6V zeners. The Control knob bends the pitch (or sets the arpeggiator speed), and a rotary switch selects normal, octave down, octave up and arpeggiator modes by grounding the chip's SW0-SW2 pins.
notes: Instead of the 4P3T rotary switch, wire three SPST switches that ground HT8950 pins 1, 2 and 3 (SW0-SW2) to select modes independently and get more range; the datasheet's switching table shows the combinations.

circuits.name: Death by Audio Supersonic Fuzz Gun
circuits.original: Death by Audio Supersonic Fuzz Gun
circuits.description: Death by Audio's extreme fuzz with fully interactive controls, from very harsh to warm. Two 2N5089 transistors wired with a strange bias and orientation (the post suggests this explains much of the crazy sound) feed a 2N5306 Darlington stage whose collector load is the Bias pot and whose emitter is the Fuzz pot, followed by a Filter and Level. A switch grounds the first two transistors' shared leg directly or through 10K to choose between gated and oscillating fuzz.

circuits.name: Demeter Compulator
circuits.description: Demeter's optical studio-style compressor: an LF353 input buffer, a VTL5C10 vactrol shunting the signal to the half-supply rail, a gain stage set by an internal trimmer, and a rectifier that drives the vactrol's LED from the output (a feedback design, which the post explains gives the illusion of extra sustain). The author has built several and recommends it.
notes: Use a real VTL5C10 or build an optocoupler that matches its specs.

circuits.name: Bajaman LA2A Style Optical Limiter rev2
circuits.description: Bajaman's own LA-2A style optical limiter built around the Compulator idea: a 2SK117 JFET input buffer, an LDR attenuator before an LF353 gain stage, and a side chain taken before the attenuator (feed-forward), so it only clamps peaks rather than adding sustain. The optocoupler is a homemade yellow LED and LDR in a sealed black tube.
notes: The LDR should read about 90 ohms in sunlight; a type reading 350 ohms or more is wrong for this project.

circuits.name: Dunlop Eric Johnson Signature Fuzz Face
circuits.original: Dunlop - Eric Johnson Signature Fuzz Face EJF1
circuits.description: Dunlop's Eric Johnson signature Fuzz Face, voiced for his violin-like sustain. The post says it is the standard two-transistor silicon Fuzz Face circuit with different values, and shows them on a photo of the board; it points to the freestompboxes.org thread where Marc Ahlfs (Skreddy) and Jeorge Tripps (Way Huge) discuss it.

circuits.name: Durham Crazy Horse
circuits.description: Durham's overdrive, boost and fuzz, inspired by Neil Young's tone. A JRC4558 op-amp stage with diode clipping in its feedback loop and a Drive control feeds a unity-gain op-amp stage and then a Fuzz Face-style transistor fuzz (two 2N2222As) with a Fuzz control on Q2's emitter, a Darlington emitter follower (MPSA13s) and a passive tone and level. A Volts control sags the supply. The author wonders why the second op amp is not used to buffer the tone section instead.

circuits.name: Fred Briggs Bliss
circuits.description: The blog author's overdrive/booster with an effects loop, designed for a friend to give old gain pedals new life: you put your gain pedal in the loop for more dynamics and warmth. A BS170 MOSFET gain stage with 1N34A germanium diodes clipping to ground feeds the FX send; the return goes through a 2N5457 JFET stage that also mixes in the MOSFET stage's source signal. Switches add bass (Bottom), set the brightness and add a Boost.

circuits.name: Fred Briggs Octave Ringmod Fuzzer (ORF)
circuits.description: The author's own octave fuzz inspired by Tim Escobedo's Tripple Fuzz: a single op amp gain stage with a bass-shaping feedback network drives a complementary PNP/NPN transistor pair (a phase splitter) whose outputs are blended through the Intensity pot for a ring-mod-like octave. Sweet at low gain and evil when pushed; it stacks well into other gain pedals.
notes: The author used a BC557 (PNP), a BC548 (NPN) and an LF351 op amp; any single op amp works.
The optional J201 gain stage (bias its drain at 5V with the 47K trimmer) adds a lot of character; the author prefers the build with it. It connects at the point marked * and takes the Volume pot.

circuits.name: Himmelstrutz Fetto
circuits.description: Himmelstrutz Elektro Art's amp-like overdrive/distortion, traced by Soulsonic (MC) with Lawnchair at freestompboxes.org. It is a JFET emulation of a tube preamp in the runoffgroove style: three cascaded JFET stages with tube-amp style coupling and bright networks, a tone section with Presence and a Mid Cut jumper, and internal jumpers and DIP switches for bass, voice, bright, gain and treble cut.
notes: The JFETs are an unknown type: the post suggests starting with 2N5257 (probably 2N5457) and keep trying types with the right pinout until they bias up nicely.
All the jumpers and DIP switches (Bass1, Bass2, Voice, Bright1, Bright2, Gain1, Gain2, Mid Cut, Treble Cut 1-3) can be brought out to the outside of the pedal for a super-adjustable overdrive.

circuits.name: Revolution Deux Invading Cannibal Ladybird
circuits.description: Fred Briggs' breadboard noisemaker that mashes together three circuits: an LM386 fuzz taken from the Experimentalists Anonymous Parallel Universe (with Starve and Oscillate switches and a Freq pot), a Big Muff tone control, and Allesz's lo-fi PT2399 delay from a freestompboxes.org circuit contest, with red LED clipping on the delay input. It makes screaming, oscillating, feedback and beeping sounds, almost a synth; the guitar's volume knob is the fuzz gain control.
notes: The author says some values need tweaking and it could do with an output buffer.
Adding modulation to the delay time (a sequencer or LFO) makes it wilder.

circuits.name: Lovepedal Amp Eleven
circuits.description: Lovepedal's Amp Eleven, an overdrive and a boost in one box on separate footswitches. The post points out that the overdrive section is essentially PaulC's Timmy (a 4558 gain stage with a Bass pot at the input, diode clipping in the feedback loop, a Tone control and a second op-amp stage), and that the boost section is just the Lovepedal COT50: a 2N5088 booster with BAT46 diodes to ground at the output.

circuits.name: Lovepedal Dragon / BBB-07 / Black Beauty Balance
circuits.description: Lovepedal's Dragon (also sold as the BBB-07, Black Beauty Balance and other names), traced by Greg on freestompboxes. It is a simple two-transistor PNP germanium Fuzz Face variant with a Blend pot at the input that sweeps between the full-range input cap and a small treble-booster style cap, so it goes from Rangemaster-like boost to Fuzz Face fuzz. The post notes the transistor types varied between versions (silicon, germanium and hybrid).
notes: The post suggests trying different transistors until you find a sound you like; versions were built with silicon, germanium and hybrid pairs.

circuits.name: Lovepedal Delux 60 Mosfet
circuits.description: A rare Lovepedal single-knob boost (also sold as the dual Twin 60): one BS170 MOSFET common-source stage with drain-to-gate feedback bias, into a volume pot. Greg notes the 0.1u/47K output high-pass was probably meant to sit near 34Hz, but the 100K volume pot in parallel with the 47K pushes it higher, and a Lovepedal Karl fuzz's 5K input after it would raise it to about 370Hz.

circuits.name: Lovepedal Englishman
circuits.description: Lovepedal's Englishman, voiced after a cranked vintage AC15/AC30. It is a single 2N5088 transistor booster derived from the EHX LPB-1, with a gain pot in the emitter and diode clipping to ground after the gain stage. The three-way Fail switch picks silicon (1N4148) diodes, BAT46 Schottky diodes or no clipping. The post notes it differs from Lovepedal's COT 50 designs only in the transistor bias and larger input and output caps.

circuits.name: Electro-Harmonix LPB-1
circuits.description: The original Electro-Harmonix LPB-1 Linear Power Booster, a single 2N5088 common-emitter stage with a volume pot on the output. The post shows it as the circuit the Englishman is mainly based on.

circuits.name: Lovepedal Kalamazoo
circuits.description: A straight Tube Screamer derivative: a 4558 clipping stage with two pairs of series 1N914 diodes in the feedback loop, then a tone stage with two controls. Tone sets the basic treble roll-off, while Glass boosts or cuts treble the way a standard Tube Screamer tone control does; the two interact slightly.
notes: The author suggests tweaking the uncertain (bracketed) values to taste.

circuits.name: Lovepedal Karl Fuzz (2-knob)
circuits.description: The older two-knob Karl: a 2N5089 gain stage, with a 5KB Intensity pot at the input, drives a 2N3906/2N3904 'non-selective frequency tripler' pair, followed by a 1N4148/BAT46 diode clipper and the Volume pot. The post identifies it as an adaptation of Tim Escobedo's Tripple Fuzz and describes it as sweet at low gain with octave and ring-mod tones at higher gain.
notes: The post says the 1M pulldown at the input is not needed, since it sits in parallel with the 5KB Intensity pot.
The post says the two power filter capacitors are unneeded and the 47u can be left out.

The newer three-knob Karl adds a tone control; the post suggests a 10n-22n capacitor to ground through a B47K pot just after the last output capacitor, before the Volume pot, or a Big Muff style tone stack.

circuits.name: Tim Escobedo Tripple Fuzz
circuits.description: Tim Escobedo's fuzz built around a 'non-selective frequency tripler', a complementary 2N3906/2N3904 pair originally designed by R. Lockhart Jr., driven by an MPSA18 gain stage and followed by silicon diode clipping. Sweet at low gain, splatty at high gain; the post shows it as the basis of the Lovepedal Karl and notes the Zvex Machine uses the same tripler.

circuits.name: Lovepedal Les Lius
circuits.description: The Lovepedal Les Lius, an overdrive voiced after vintage Fender amps, with a three-way switch for 5E3 Woody, High Power Twin and Master Volume Tchula modes. The post identifies it as another variation of the Electra Distortion (like the Lovepedal COT 50 and Woodrow): a single 2N5088 gain stage with an emitter gain pot, followed by switchable silicon and Schottky clipping diodes and a volume pot. A JFET switched by SW2 shorts the gain pot's emitter path for the boost function.
notes: The JFET switching for the boost function is unnecessary and can be replaced with a simple switch, as the vero layout does (S2, SPST, or DPDT for an LED).

circuits.name: Lovepedal OD Eleven
circuits.description: Lovepedal's transparent overdrive with separate Bass and Tone controls, runnable from 9 to 18V. The trace shows it is PaulC's Timmy with a few value changes, and the same as the overdrive side of the Lovepedal Amp Eleven: a JRC4558 gain stage with two pairs of series 1N4148s in its feedback loop and a Bass control in the gain leg, then a passive Tone low-pass and a gain-of-two recovery stage.

circuits.name: Lovepedal Super 6
circuits.description: An old Lovepedal design meant to give a Blackface Fender Super 'on 6' tone. It is a single BS170 MOSFET common-source stage with drain-to-gate feedback bias and a 9.1V zener from gate to source, with an Intense pot setting how much the source resistor is bypassed; the MOSFET's own soft clipping does the work without diodes. A simple low-pass 'vintage tone stack' (a pot bridged by a cap) and a Volume pot follow. It departs from Lovepedal's usual Electra/LPB booster formula.
notes: The author prefers a 390R in place of the 510R source resistor (R5) for a little more gain, a 22n input cap (C1) instead of 100n, and a 100n output cap (C2) instead of 10n.

circuits.name: Lovepedal Superlead
circuits.description: A Guitar Center exclusive that turns out to be a Marshall Guv'nor without its tone stack: a 4558 non-inverting gain stage with the Drive pot, a second inverting stage, then a two-way Mids switch choosing silicon diodes or red LEDs as clippers to ground, a simple Tone control and Level.

circuits.name: Mad Professor Blueberry Bass Overdrive
circuits.description: The Mad Professor Blueberry Bass Overdrive, which the post says is based on the BJF Honey Bee circuit. A BF244A JFET input stage feeds a CA3130 op-amp with LED clipping in its feedback loop and a Drive pot, then a passive filter with a diode pair, and a second BF244A output stage. The Nature control blends signal from the output stage's source back into the op-amp's feedback network.

circuits.name: Mad Professor Deep Blue Delay
circuits.description: The Mad Professor Deep Blue Delay, reverse engineered and drawn by madbeanpedals as the Sea Urchin. The post says there is nothing new in it: a standard PT2399 digital delay based on the Rebote 2.5, with a TL072 input buffer and output mixer, but it sounds very good.

circuits.name: Mad Professor Forest Green Compressor
circuits.description: An optical compressor whose basic building block is the Ibanez CP-830: an AD797 op-amp stage with an LDR and the Comp pot in its feedback loop, a BC550C side chain with a 1N914 rectifier driving the LDR's LED, and a 2SK170 JFET / BC560C output stage. A switch selects compressor or sustain mode, and a Tone control fine-tunes the compressed sound.
notes: The drawing lists a second set of values ('FGC_CB_VALUES') for another board version: op-amp JRC5534DD with 100p between pins 5 and 8, C1 22n, C5 100n, C6 1u, C8 4u7, C12 1u, C15 1u, C16 100u, R5 43K, R7 4K3, R8 7K5, R9 51K, R11 14K7 (queried), R19 33K, R23 215R, R25 5K6, R27 51K.
That board version uses a different tone circuit: two 20KA pots ('Tone' A and B) on a dual control.
ShortScaleMike's vero (image 7) is unverified; the post asks builders to report back.

circuits.name: Mad Professor Ruby Red Booster
circuits.description: Bjorn Juhl's design for Mad Professor: a BJF Little Red Trebler treble booster followed by a Red Rooster booster with a master volume, built from four 2N5952 JFET stages. It can serve as treble booster, clean boost or overdrive. An internal switch adds a JRC5534 op-amp buffer that stays on in bypass, or leaves the pedal true bypass.

circuits.name: Mad Professor Sky Blue Overdrive (with mods)
circuits.description: Bjorn Juhl's (BJF) four-knob overdrive for Mad Professor, meant to push already distorted amps or give light drive on a clean one. An OP275 gain stage with LED clippers is followed by an unusual 'Texture' network of two 2N3819 JFETs that changes how and when the circuit distorts and its EQ, and a 'Z' pot that sets the load on the guitar pickups.
notes: Mictester's Texture mod (drawn here) works like the original control but needs only a single pot instead of a dual-gang one.
The Texture pot can be raised to 5K B for a more useful range (mictester's suggestion).

circuits.name: Mad Professor Stone Grey Distortion
circuits.description: Mad Professor's high-gain Stone Grey Distortion, taken apart on freestompboxes.org and drawn by RoseBlood11. A TL051 op-amp gain stage, with two diode-connected 2N3819 JFETs in its feedback loop and a 1M Distortion pot, drives two CD4069UBE CMOS inverter stages into clipping (the post credits their MOSFET innards for the sound), followed by a simple tone control and volume.

circuits.name: 1970s Japanese textbook CMOS overdrive
circuits.description: A schematic from a 1970s Japanese electronics textbook with the same structure as the Stone Grey: an LF356 op-amp gain stage driving two MC14049B CMOS inverter stages into clipping. Its controls differ: an Amplitude pot sets the op-amp gain, an Over Drive pot sets the drive into the first inverter, and a Bias pot shifts the first inverter's operating point. The author thinks the dual gain control and the bias control are worth exploring.
notes: The author found it wanted a little less treble and more bass, and suggests experimenting with the bias control.

circuits.name: MI Audio Crunch Box (V1)
circuits.description: The early version of MI Audio's high-gain Crunch Box distortion: two LM833 op-amp gain stages, a pair of red LEDs clipping to ground, then a simple tone control and volume. The post notes it is essentially a Marshall Guv'nor without the three-band tone stack, much like the Lovepedal Superlead.

circuits.name: MI Audio Crunch Box (V2)
circuits.description: The later version of the MI Audio Crunch Box, with the internal Presence control MI Audio describes. It keeps the two LM833 gain stages and LED clipping of V1 but changes the tone network: 470 ohm after the second stage, a 22n tone cap and a 20K presence trimmer in place of the 10K/4.7K output divider.
notes: Presence (VR4) is an internal 20K trimmer on the original; the turretboard.org layout brings it out as a fourth pot.

circuits.name: Marshall Guv'nor
circuits.description: Michael Burgundy's 1999 drawing of the Marshall Guv'nor, shown in the post as the circuit the Crunch Box is based on: a TL072 with two gain stages, red LED clipping to ground, a three-band passive tone stack and an effects loop.

circuits.name: OKKO Diablo Boost+
circuits.description: A low-to-medium gain overdrive built from cascaded JFET stages in the style of Jack Orman's Booster 2.5 / Microbooster, with a Feed control for the bass going into the drive and a Body control for mids and compression. The Boost+ adds an extra JFET boost stage (the '+' knob), and a Headroom switch turns on a voltage doubler to run the circuit at about 18V.
notes: Harald Sabro's layouts leave out the voltage doubler; the post shows an LTC1044/ICL7660S positive doubler (image 5: IC1 with D1, D2 1N5817, C1 10u, C2 100u) and a switch to choose between +9V and about +18V.
The layouts suggest 2N5457 or similar JFETs as substitutes for the J201s.
Use a DPDT or 3PDT between the main board and the boost stage to switch the boost in and out.

circuits.name: AMZ Booster 2.5
circuits.description: Jack Orman's Booster 2.5 (with modifications by Dron Nelson): two cascaded JFET mu-amp stages with a Drive pot between them and a passive tone control before the volume. The post shows it because the OKKO Diablo's schematic follows the same cascaded Microbooster formula, also used in the Catalinbread Dirty Little Secret and Formula No. 5.
notes: The drawing notes that the two 100 ohm source resistors can be 1K for a milder overdrive.

circuits.name: OKKO Dominator
circuits.description: A German high-gain distortion in the same league as the Wampler Triple Wreck. Two BF245A JFET stages feed a pair of cascaded op amp gain stages that run from a doubled, regulated supply (ICL7660S charge pump and 78L15) and do the clipping themselves, followed by an active three-band EQ whose mid frequency is set by a three-position Mid Range switch. The post notes it is an op amp clipper running at a higher voltage than usual.

circuits.name: Penny Pedals Fingerprint
circuits.description: An NJM386 power-amp-chip distortion made with artist Laura Bennett. Its Texture control is a diode feedback path from the output back to the input that pushes the chip toward oscillation: low settings give normal distortion, higher settings get fuzzier and gated, and full gain with full texture gives glitchy octave fuzz. The output is clipped by a 1N4148 and an LED to ground.
notes: Newer Fingerprint pedals have a switch that bypasses the Gain pot to full gain.
The post says the NJM386 is important to the sound.

circuits.name: Experimentalists Anonymous Parallel Universe (old version)
circuits.description: Colin Raffel's LM386 gain-driven oscillator, given in the post as a related, more versatile 386 design. A Gate switch starves the chip's supply through a 1k pot or a 2k2 resistor, and an Oscillate switch adds a cap and Freq pot between pins 5 and 7 so the chip oscillates at a rate set by the signal level and the pot.
notes: The 1k gain pot gives a small range and 5k is too big (per the drawing).
The tone cap can be .047 or .1uF; a lower value gives less top cut.
The drawing marks the 47k / Level / Tone section as a volume stage that you may replace with something better.

circuits.name: Experimentalists Anonymous Parallel Universe (revised)
circuits.description: Colin Raffel's 2006 revision of the Parallel Universe: a TL072 input amplifier with a gain of 3 and an output buffer around the LM386 oscillating fuzz, a wider-range gain control, an effects send and return between the input amp and the LM386, Mark Hammer's 'stupidly wonderful' tone and level control, and a better Freq control. It ranges from Big Muff-like overdrive to loud oscillating fuzz.
notes: R7 can be lowered for more gain in the input amp.
C7 sets the upper frequency of the Freq pot and C8 the lower.
Send and Return are switched mono jacks; wire them together if you want no effects loop, or feed the Return to skip the input amplifier.
It only oscillates with the gain knob turned up; otherwise the oscillation just makes crazy fuzz.

circuits.name: Rockbox Boiling Point
circuits.description: A $350 boutique overdrive that the freestompboxes forum found to be a Tube Screamer 808 clone with a few mods: MPSA18 input and output buffers, a 4558 gain stage with a detented A1M Drive pot, a clipping switch choosing between LED clipping and pairs of 1N4148s, and a bass switch that changes the cap in the gain stage's ground leg.

circuits.name: mictester Simplified Klon Centaur
circuits.description: mictester's single-rail version of the Klon Centaur: the same circuit as the original without the charge pump, with each section adjusted so its response matches an original unit, and tested against originals. It keeps the dual-gang Gain pot that blends the clean path with the 1N34A germanium-clipped path, the active treble control and the buffered output, with a 1N4742 zener on the supply.

circuits.name: Wampler Plexi-Drive
circuits.description: Brian Wampler's Marshall Plexi-in-a-box: three cascaded J201 common-source stages with the Gain pot between the first and second, followed by a two-pole RC low-pass and a simple Tone control to ground ahead of the Volume pot. A switch (S2) adds a 2.2n cap in parallel with the first coupling cap for more low end. Traced by the freestompboxes.org community, with input from Brian himself.

circuits.name: Wampler Triple Wreck
circuits.description: Wampler's very high-gain distortion, often compared to a 5150 amp. A TL074 runs an input buffer, two cascaded gain stages, diode clipping to ground and a feedback-clipping stage, followed by a passive treble and bass stack; a TL072 then adds a recovery stage and an active mid control. A switch selects the Vintage (warmer) or Modern (brighter) voice.

circuits.name: Xotic BB Preamp
circuits.description: Xotic's BB Preamp, a boost/overdrive with up to 30dB of clean boost, a pre-gain stage and an active two-band (bass and treble) EQ. The post sums it up as an op-amp clipping stage into a tone and boost section: a 2N5088 input buffer, a JRC4558 gain stage with diode clipping, and a TL072 active EQ and output stage.

circuits.name: Xotic EP Booster
circuits.description: Xotic's boost said to be based on the Echoplex EP-3 preamp, though the traced circuit does not much resemble it: a JFET gain stage whose source bypass is set by the Boost pot, a switchable passive low-pass filter, and a BJT emitter-follower output. Internal DIP switches choose the boost voicing and EQ.
notes: The author would run it at 18V, replace the drain resistor with a 25k trimmer to find a sweet spot, swap the low-pass filter for Mark Hammer's Stupidly Wonderful Tone Control, and use a JFET or MOSFET follower in place of the BJT output buffer.
To reduce the low end, lower the input cap to 33nF and change the bypass cap on the Boost control to 220nF-1uF to taste.
Replace the first JFET's drain resistor with a 10k trimmer and set 5.5V on the drain.

circuits.name: Xotic EP Booster - Fred Briggs Mods
circuits.description: The author's version of the EP Booster: the same 2N5457 gain stage with the Boost pot on the source, a treble roll-off Tone control (which could be called 'Sparkle'), a master Volume, and a JFET source follower in place of the BJT output. The bass boost switch is left out, and an ICL7660S doubler lets it run at 18V, where it sounds best, from a 9V battery.
notes: The bass boost switch was omitted because it muddied the boost; it can be added back.
To reduce the low end, lower the input cap to 33nF and change the bypass cap on the Boost control to 220nF-1uF to taste.
Replace the first JFET's drain resistor with a 10k trimmer and set 5.5V on the drain.

circuits.name: Fred Briggs EQ Booster (prototype)
circuits.description: A 2009 prototype by the author of a coloring booster: a 2N5457 gain stage with a Bass control in the input network and a treble control after it, followed by a second 2N5457 stage into the Level pot. He says it sounds best at 18V and the treble control values still need tweaking.
notes: The values in the treble control need tweaking to find the best response.
The 100K drain trimmer can probably be replaced with a 10K trimmer; set both drains to 5.5V.

circuits.name: ZVex Box of Metal (without the gate)
circuits.description: A high-gain distortion made of five cascaded BS170 MOSFET gain stages in the Super Hard On style, followed by a passive Treble/Mid/Bass tone stack and a Volume control. The schematic and the madbean Kokbox project leave out the original's noise gate section, which was deemed unnecessary. The trace is credited to CultureJam and Bajaman on freestompboxes.

circuits.name: ZVex Box of Rock
circuits.description: ZVex's Marshall-style overdrive: three cascaded BS170 MOSFET stages in the style of the ZVex Super Hard On, with a Big Muff style tone control whose values come from the Brown Sound in a Box II, followed by a separate footswitched Super Hard On style boost. An ex-Madbean project.

circuits.name: Zvex Super Duper 2-in-1
circuits.description: Two cascaded Zvex Super Hard-On channels in one box, each a single BS170 MOSFET common-source stage with a 9.1V zener protecting the gate and a 5K gain (Level) rheostat in the source. Channel 2's output bleeder resistor is replaced by a 100K Master volume so the pair can be used as an overdrive at any output level. Each channel has its own footswitch.
notes: Use 3PDT switches instead of DPDT to add LED indicators.
The post suggests building two Super Hard-On layouts, or Madbean's FireBomb project, for a board.

circuits.name: ZVex Super Hard On (MKII)
circuits.description: A single BS170 MOSFET booster with a very high input impedance, a 9.1V zener from gate to source and a reverse-log 5K pot in the source that sets the gain (the 'Crackle Okay' control). The post quotes Estragon's analysis: the source pot moves the drain voltage from about 7.2V to 4V, the gain from 0 to almost 40 dB, and the input impedance from 3.3M down to 140K.
notes: The drawing says almost every component can be altered; experiment.
IvIark's vero places the zener slightly differently; the post says it makes no difference to the tone.

circuits.name: Soulsonic Crackle Not OK
circuits.description: Soulsonic's variation on the Super Hard On: the BS170 source goes straight to ground and the gain is set instead by a 1M 'Crackle' pot in series between the input cap and the gate, with 2M2 bias resistors. The post describes it as a Super Hard On without the crackling gain pot.

circuits.name: FrequencyCentral Superheated SHO #1
circuits.description: Rick Holt's (FrequencyCentral) take on the Super Hard On: a switch replaces the 5K1 drain resistor with a 2N5457 JFET current source, turning the BS170 booster into a mu-amp. The post warns it is seriously loud.

circuits.name: Landgraff Clean Boost (drawn by Clay Jones)
circuits.description: Clay Jones's drawing of the Landgraff Clean Boost, which the post points out is a Zvex Super Hard On MKI: an NTE490 N-channel MOSFET with 10M bias resistors, 1N914 protection diodes and a 5K linear source pot with 10 detents.
notes: The drawing lists a yellow AVX box input cap, a brown Nichicon filter cap, a Sprague output electrolytic, 1/4W carbon comp resistors and a Hammond 1590B box.

circuits.name: B K Butler Tube Driver (early garage-made version)
circuits.description: A hand-drawn trace of an early (around 1979-80) B K Butler Tube Driver, the pedal Butler first built in his garage. A 4558 op-amp input buffer and gain stage drive both halves of a 12AX7 run from a split +13V/-14V supply, followed by a passive Hi/Lo tone stack and output level, all powered from a 24VAC center-tapped transformer.
notes: The tracer notes that C2 should be non-polarized; replace it with a film cap when possible (the reissue fixes this).
The tracer notes that the main difference between this version and the newer one is R14, which goes from 2.2K here to 22K on the new one.
V1 can be a 12AX7, 12AT7 or 12AU7. The tracer suggests rewiring it for true bypass.

circuits.name: B K Butler Tube Driver Rev 2 (bajaman)
circuits.description: bajaman's verified and working project traced from a reissue B K Butler Tube Driver. A TL072 input buffer and gain stage (Tube Drive) feed a 12AX7 with both halves cascaded, then a passive Hi/Lo tone stack and output level, powered from a 12VAC transformer with split rails. It adds a Bias pot on the tube cathodes that shifts the grid voltages and changes the character of the clipping.
notes: The Bias mod (10K linear pot on the shared cathode) lets you alter the voltages seen on the tube's grid, which changes the character of the clipping.

circuits.name: Barber Dirty Bomb
circuits.description: A high-gain distortion that the post identifies as basically a Marshall Shredmaster with MOSFET clipping: a TL074 gain stage with the Gain pot in its feedback, a second gain stage, 2N7000 MOSFETs (with 1N4148s) as clippers, a Shredmaster-style Bass/Treble stack with a mid-character toggle, and an internal Sub-Bass control in the output stage.
notes: The post suggests building a Marshall Shredmaster with switchable diode clipping options instead.

circuits.name: Colorsound Power Boost (early version)
circuits.description: The late-1960s Colorsound Power Boost, run from 18V: three silicon transistors (BC169C, BC184C or BC109): a two-transistor high-gain preamp with a 10k pot in the first stage's emitter, a Baxandall bass and treble stack, and a third transistor recovery stage. Colorsound's own text says it and the Overdriver are the same circuit in a different case; turned up full it is the classic Beck/Gilmour overdrive.

circuits.name: Colorsound Power Boost (later version)
circuits.description: A later 18V Colorsound Power Boost: three silicon transistors (BC169C, BC184C or BC109): a two-transistor high-gain preamp with a 10k pot in the first stage's emitter, a Baxandall bass and treble stack, and a third transistor recovery stage. It differs from the early version in its coupling and bypass capacitors (10u instead of 4.7u, a 220n output cap) and has no 10k output resistor.

circuits.name: Colorsound Overdriver
circuits.description: The Overdriver, the Power Boost rehoused in a grey hammerite case for the American market and the pedal Jeff Beck used on Blow by Blow. This version runs on 9V: three silicon transistors (BC169C, BC184C or BC109): a two-transistor high-gain preamp with a 10k pot in the first stage's emitter, a Baxandall bass and treble stack, and a third transistor recovery stage. The recovery stage uses 150k/1k8/470 bias values instead of the 18V version's 180k/3k9/1k.
notes: The vero layout adds an optional 1M input pull-down resistor (R15 on the layout).
The vero layout shows an optional 100k volume control on the output.
The vero builder adjusted the two 1k8 collector resistors (to 2k) to give 5V on the collectors; the reissue uses a 2k2 Gain pot and different capacitor values (layout color key).

circuits.name: Sola Sound Tone Bender MKII Professional
circuits.description: The Sola Sound / Colorsound Tone Bender MKII Professional, a three-transistor germanium fuzz with huge gain and sustain, the sound of Jimmy Page's Led Zeppelin I era. Sola Sound also built it for Vox (Tone Bender Professional MKII), Marshall (Supa Fuzz) and Rotosound. A single germanium input stage feeds a direct-coupled pair with feedback from the output collector, positive ground on a -9V supply.
notes: Recommended gains: Q1 about 70 hFE, Q2 70-90 hFE, Q3 100-120 hFE.
Always use a germanium transistor for Q1; Q2 and Q3 can be experimented with using low-gain silicon transistors.

circuits.name: Dunlop JH-F1 Jimi Hendrix Fuzz Face
circuits.original: Dunlop JH-F1 Jimi Hendrix Fuzz Face
circuits.description: Dunlop's Hendrix-branded Fuzz Face, a two-transistor silicon Fuzz Face on a negative-ground 9V supply with BC108 transistors matched around 260 hFE. Trimmers in both collector loads set the bias (Q1 collector 1.35V, Q2 collector 5.75V), and a small cap between Q1's base and Q2's emitter tames the highs. The post says it builds on any standard Fuzz Face layout with the right substitutions.
notes: R4 may be 5.11K on early units.
The trimmers are probably interactive, so check both collector voltages when biasing; 20K and 1K trimmers (or values between those and the ones drawn) would also work.

circuits.name: Fred Briggs '64
circuits.description: The blog author's own single-transistor overdrive aiming at 1960s Vox tones, a heavily modified Electro-Harmonix LPB-1 that starts from the Lovepedal Englishman. A 4.7K collector resistor adds gain, an 82n emitter bypass cap and a 47K/22n filter at the output push the upper mids, and an SB340 Schottky plus BAT46 give asymmetrical clipping whose amount the Headroom control sets, with a tube-like sag as it is rolled back.
notes: The 2N3565 sounded best in tests, but a 2N5088, BC108 or any decent-gain NPN can be used.
The finished pedal adds a diode switch (as on the Lovepedal Englishman) in series with the Headroom control, selecting the BAT46/SB340 pair, 1N4148s or no diodes.

circuits.name: Fred Briggs Dual Band Vibrato "Bliss"
circuits.description: The author's own design: an op-amp buffer splits the signal into a treble path (high-passed around 900Hz) and a bass path (low-passed around 1000Hz), each through a transistor phase-splitter stage with an LDR in the emitter, as in a Uni-Vibe stage. Each band gets its own LFO (phase-shift oscillator driving an LED onto that band's LDR), so depth and speed can be set per band; the overlap of the bands gives pseudo phase-shifting, from plain vibrato to an almost Uni-Vibe sound. A Mix pot blends the bands into an output gain stage.
notes: Use two LFOs, one for each band; only one is drawn.
The Mix pot can be B47K or B100K.
The author likes the bass band on a slow vibrato with the treble band fast; the project was still in progress when posted.

circuits.name: Fred Briggs E11even
circuits.description: Fred Briggs' Marshall-flavored booster/overdrive (plexi and JTM45 tones), the last of his Fender/Vox/Marshall themed series. It is a single BS170 MOSFET booster with a Body pot in the input filter that sets the bass content (at 470k it is close to the classic Marshall mid/high boost filter), a Gain pot in the source leg, and a pair of BAT41 clipping diodes fed through a Bias pot that acts as a saturation control: high for headroom and a smoother drive, low for a grittier tone.
notes: Suggested mod: put the Bias (saturation) control over one diode only for asymmetrical clipping.
The protection diode can be a 12V zener or a red LED.
The author uses a 470k linear pot for Body; a log taper may suit some players.

circuits.name: Fred Briggs 'Face MKI
circuits.description: The author's own Fender-voiced booster/overdrive: two stacked JFETs in an SRPP-style stage, inspired by a 1943 patent, a 1997 microphone preamp and Tim Escobedo's Syrupp Booster, with diode clipping and an onboard charge pump for up to 18V. Lower supply voltage gives less gain and clipping, more gives more.
notes: Supply can be 4.5-18V; the lower the voltage the less gain and clipping.
2N5457 JFETs give more gain and a more compressed sound (tweed); MPF102s give more headroom and less gain (Twin). 2N5458 and J201 also work; the author found J201s too compressed and fuzzy.
Use a larger tone cap than 3n3 for a darker tone, a smaller one for more high-end drive. The author's build used MPF102s at 18V with a 4n7 tone cap.
Adjust the 4K7 trimmer for the best tone.

circuits.name: Fred Briggs 'Face MKII "Fender Tone Deluxe"
circuits.description: The version of the 'Face the author built: the same stacked-MPF102 stage with a reworked tone control (a 33n cap to ground through a 100KA pot) that he finds works better with MPF102s, switchable diode clipping, and a MAX1044 doubler with a 12V zener. He describes it as a 'cranked Twin' tone, dynamic, keeping its low end and fizzing out at higher gain.
notes: Adjust the 4K7 trimmer for the best tone.

circuits.name: Fred Briggs Super OCD
circuits.description: The author's expanded Fulltone OCD (itself based on the Voodoo Lab Overdrive): an OPA2134 gain stage into a pair of 2N7000/BS170 MOSFET clippers, then a second op-amp stage set up as a clean boost, a tone control and volume. It adds a pre-gain Bass control borrowed from Paul C's Timmy, a Saturation pot that raises the clipping headroom, the Boost control, and a switch between 9V and 18V from a MAX1044 doubler.
notes: The 10K-15K resistor after the gain stage: choose the value that suits your gear.
The tone cap can be anything from 22n to 68n; a larger value gives a darker tone.
Low-voltage-drop diodes can replace the 1N4001s in the voltage doubler.

circuits.name: Boss SD-1 Super Overdrive
circuits.description: Boss's Super Overdrive, which the post describes as a Tube Screamer derivative with a few substituted values. A transistor input buffer feeds a dual op amp clipping stage with asymmetric diode clipping (two diodes one way, one the other) in the feedback loop, then the tone stage and a transistor output buffer, with the usual Boss JFET switching. Part of a guide to building a Jonny Greenwood (Radiohead, 1995-97) style pedalboard.

circuits.name: Demeter Tremulator
circuits.description: An optical tremolo. A dual op amp LFO (with zener diodes limiting its swing) drives an LED/LDR optocoupler through a buffer, and the optocoupler shunts the signal after a unity-gain op amp stage to vary the volume. The post says Jonny Greenwood used one and that the layout can also be built as a Fulltone Supa-Trem, which it calls a copy of the Tremulator with a few mods.
notes: The layout notes say: leave out the hard/soft switch for a basic two-knob Tremulator, and add a 47u or 100u filter capacitor at the 9V jack for noise filtering.
The layout can also be built as a Fulltone Supa-Trem.

circuits.name: Forced Fire Pedals Magnus Modulus
circuits.description: A PT2399 echo designed by Nathan Alexander Smith (FF_Pedals, 2008), adapted from the PT2399 datasheet, the Tonepad Rebote, the BYOC Ping Pong, the Tremulus Lune and the Echo Base. An op amp LFO modulates the delay time for chorus, vibrato and tape-flutter effects and can also drive a JFET for tremolo; the post suggests it as a DIY stand-in for the Roland Space Echo, including self-oscillation.
notes: The three 240k LFO resistors can be 220k instead (shown in red on the drawing).
The Rate and Depth pots can be C taper instead of B.
The 100 ohm resistor before the Rate pot can be replaced with a B1K pot for a fine rate control.

circuits.name: Joyo Ultimate Drive (Harley Benton Ultimate Drive)
circuits.description: The Joyo Ultimate Drive, sold as the Harley Benton Ultimate Drive and repainted as the Freakish Blues Alpha Drive, is a budget copy of the Fulltone OCD (itself close to the Voodoo Lab Overdrive). A TL082 non-inverting gain stage with a 1M Drive pot feeds 2N7000 MOSFET and germanium-diode clippers to Vref, then a second gain stage, a passive tone control and a two-position output filter switch.

circuits.name: Keeley Katana Boost
circuits.description: Keeley's Katana clean boost: two cascaded 2N5458 common-source JFET stages run at 18V from an ICL7660S charge pump, which doubles the gain of the same circuit at 9V. A push-pull switch on the volume pot adds a 10uF bypass cap across the first stage's source resistor and a 15n cap to ground at the output for a fatter, overdriven mode. The post says the bypassed mode brings in its own clipping and the author prefers it without.
notes: Use a smaller cap than 10uF across the first source resistor for a treble and mid boost instead of a full one.
Replace the 4.7K drain resistors with 10K trimmers and bias each JFET's drain to about half the supply (about 9V).

circuits.name: Klon Buffer
circuits.description: The buffer section of the Klon Centaur on its own: half a TL072 as a unity-gain voltage follower biased at half supply, with a 560 ohm series output resistor. The post explains that a buffer counters the high-end loss ('tone suck') from long cables, many true-bypass pedals or low-impedance effects such as fuzzes and wahs.

circuits.name: ProCo The Rat (early version, 1986 trace)
circuits.description: A schematic of an early ProCo RAT traced in 1986 from an actual unit: an LM308 op-amp gain stage with hard-clipping 1N4148 diodes to ground, a passive Filter control and a 2N5458 JFET output buffer. Part of a post on building Kurt Cobain's Nevermind-era pedalboard; the author prefers the RAT to the DS-1 for its more open, less nasal tone.
notes: The clipping diodes are a big part of the RAT sound: the 1N4148s can be swapped for almost anything (the author likes red LEDs; MOSFETs wired as diodes also sound good). For the Nirvana tone keep the 1N4148s.

circuits.name: Electro-Harmonix Big Muff Pi
circuits.description: Phillip Bryant's reference drawing of the classic four-transistor Electro-Harmonix Big Muff Pi: an input gain stage, two diode-clipping gain stages, the passive Big Muff tone stack and a recovery stage. The post includes it as the Big Muff Kurt Cobain used while recording Nevermind, praising its smooth, compressed distortion.

circuits.name: Rick Holt Little Angel MKII Mini Chorus
circuits.description: A simple chorus designed by Rick Holt (August 2010) and enhanced by Mictester (April 2011) at freestompboxes.org, built around the common PT2399 delay chip instead of the obsolete MN3007 bucket brigade. A TL074 handles the input buffer, mixing, output stage and the LFO, which modulates the PT2399 clock through a 2N3904. The post offers it as an easier alternative to the Electro-Harmonix Small Clone that Kurt Cobain used.
notes: An even simpler version using a single dual op-amp is in the Little Angel thread on freestompboxes.org.

circuits.name: Lovepedal Black Magic Distortion
circuits.description: An early, short-lived Lovepedal distortion aimed at the Eddie Van Halen 'brown sound'. It is a very simple LM386 power-amp-chip distortion, with the Dist pot setting the gain between pins 8 and 1 through a 47u cap; some say it is based on Aron Nelson's Smash Drive. The author does not like it: the distortion is crackly and the decay gated.

circuits.name: Aron Nelson Smash Drive
circuits.description: Aron Nelson's 2002 LM386 distortion (Rev B, from diystompboxes.com), shown in the post because some think the Black Magic is derived from it. The LM386's gain is set by a 5K Drive pot and 100 ohm resistor with a 47u cap between pins 8 and 1, and the output goes either through a plain coupling cap (Version A) or a passive Treble/Bass/Mid tone stack (Version B) to a 500K volume pot.
notes: Simple Version A replaces the tone stack with a 100n film cap from pin 5 to the volume pot; Killer Version B uses the three-knob tone stack listed here.

circuits.name: Nick Greer Ghetto Stomp
circuits.description: Greer's three-knob overdrive aimed at tweed and Valco style amp breakup. As traced by soniciv it is another Electra Distortion derivative: a single 2N3904 gain stage with collector feedback, a Gain pot as an input attenuator, a pair of silicon clipping diodes to ground, then Volume and a simple treble-cut Tone.

circuits.name: Greer Amps Sucker Punch
circuits.description: Nick Greer's high-gain distortion, sold as a preamp plus 'power amp' design voiced after a dying vintage Marshall Lead. The trace shows a J201 JFET booster with a trimmer on the drain feeding the Gain pot and an LM386 power amp chip that does the distortion, followed by the Volume pot and a simple treble-cut Tone control. The post's author is not a fan of 386 distortions because of their note decay.

circuits.name: Pete Cornish LD-1 Buffer
circuits.description: The discrete class A input buffer Pete Cornish puts in all his pedals (he is against true bypass) and sells on its own as the LD-1 line driver. It is a single BC549 emitter follower with a bootstrapped bias network for a high input impedance, a 1n cap across the base for RF filtering, a 10M input pulldown and a 51R series output resistor.

circuits.name: Skreddy Lunar Module
circuits.description: Marc Ahlfs' fuzz voiced for the guitar solos on Dark Side of the Moon: a BC109C preamp stage with a pregain trim feeding a silicon Fuzz Face-style pair (BC109Cs) with a reverse-log Gain pot in the emitter, a pre-distortion bass control and a post-distortion treble filter. The post says it is basically Skreddy's Screwdriver with part substitutions, and that Marc's careful parts choices matter to the sound.

circuits.name: Skreddy Lunar Module Deluxe
